sections.title: Welcome to LumeCard
sections.content: LumeCard is a cross-platform flashcard application designed to help you learn effectively using spaced repetition. It works offline on Android, Windows, Linux, and macOS.

sections.title: Creating Your First Card
items: Launch the app and tap the + button on the bottom bar
Select a deck from the list, or create a new one by tapping 'New Deck'
Enter the question on the front side and the answer on the back side
Optionally add tags to help organize your cards
Tap 'Save' to add the card to your deck

sections.content: You can use keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+N to create a new card, Ctrl+S to save, and Ctrl+Enter to quickly save and create another.
On first launch, the app automatically creates a sample knowledge base with 4 decks and 18 cards covering all 7 card types. You can freely delete the demo data.

sections.title: Starting Your First Study Session
sections.content: Once you have created at least one deck with cards, tap the 'Study' button on the deck to start a study session. LumeCard will present cards based on their review schedule. Rate your recall using the Again, Hard, Good, and Easy buttons.
Your first few days will feel light as new cards are introduced gradually based on your daily new card limit (default 20). You can adjust this in Settings.

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.content: The Dashboard is your home screen. It shows your daily progress, study statistics, and quick access to recent decks and learning plans.

sections.title: Navigating the App
items: Bottom bar: Quick access to Home, Study, Decks, Stats, and Settings
Swipe left/right on cards during review to see additional info
Tap the ⋮ menu on a deck to delete it
Use the search icon to find cards across all decks

sections.title: Study Session
sections.content: During a study session, cards are shown one at a time. After viewing the question, tap or press a key to reveal the answer. Rate your recall: Again (forgot), Hard (difficult), Good (normal), Easy (trivial). Your rating determines when the card will appear again.

items.question: How are new cards scheduled?
items.answer: New cards are shown up to your daily limit (default 20). They appear interleaved with review cards based on the review mode setting.

items.question: What happens if I skip a day?
items.answer: Review cards accumulate. The scheduler will show a backlog based on your daily review limit. You can increase the limit temporarily to catch up.

items.question: Can I study offline?
items.answer: Yes! LumeCard works fully offline. WebDAV sync is only needed for backup or multi-device use.

sections.title: Card Types
sections.content: LumeCard supports multiple card types: Basic (front and back), Reversed (auto-generates reverse card), Cloze (fill-in-the-blank), Multiple Choice, Markdown, and Rich Text.

sections.title: Editing a Card
items: Navigate to the deck containing the card
Tap the card to open its detail view
Tap the edit icon (pencil) to modify the content
Make your changes and tap Save

sections.content: Deleting a card is permanent. Deleted cards are removed from all review schedules and cannot be recovered. Consider suspending cards instead if you want to temporarily hide them.

sections.title: Tags and Organization
sections.content: Tags help you filter and find cards. You can add multiple tags per card. Use the search bar on the card list screen to filter by tags: type 'tag:grammar' to show only cards with the 'grammar' tag.
You can export cards to CSV format for backup or bulk editing. Go to Settings > Data Management > Export Data.

sections.title: Knowledge Bases
sections.content: Knowledge Bases (KBs) are top-level containers that group related decks. For example, you might have a 'Japanese' KB and a 'Programming' KB, each containing their own decks.

sections.title: Decks
sections.content: Decks are collections of cards on a specific topic. Each deck belongs to a knowledge base. You can customize a deck's color and icon for visual identification.

sections.title: Creating a New Deck
items: Go to the Decks tab from the bottom bar
Tap the + button or 'New Deck'
Enter a name for the deck
Optionally select or create a parent knowledge base
Choose a color and icon
Tap Save to create the deck

sections.content: Deleting a deck will permanently delete ALL cards within it. This action cannot be undone. Before deleting, consider exporting the deck as a backup.
Moving a deck to a different knowledge base will update all its cards' association. Study progress is preserved.

sections.title: AI-Powered Card Generation
sections.content: LumeCard can generate flashcards automatically using AI providers. You can input source text and let AI create well-structured cards with questions and answers.

sections.title: Setting Up AI
items: Go to Settings > AI Config
Select a provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or custom) and enter your API key
Configure the model and parameters (temperature, max tokens)
Save the configuration

sections.content: You can customize the AI prompt to control the format and style of generated cards. Edit the prompt in the AI Configuration screen.

sections.title: Using AI Card Generation
sections.content: Navigate to the AI Card screen and paste your source material. You can generate single cards or batches. The system will parse the AI response and create cards that you can review and save.
AI-generated cards should always be reviewed before saving. The AI may occasionally produce incorrect or poorly structured content. Verify each card before adding it to your study queue.

items.question: Which AI providers are supported?
items.answer: OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-3.5), Anthropic (Claude), and any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.

items.question: Are my API keys stored securely?
items.answer: Yes, API keys are stored in the app's local settings database and never transmitted to third parties.

items.question: Can I use AI without internet?
items.answer: No, AI features require an internet connection to communicate with the provider's API.

sections.title: What is WebDAV Sync?
sections.content: WebDAV sync allows you to back up your data to a cloud server and synchronize across multiple devices. LumeCard supports any WebDAV-compatible service.

sections.title: Setting Up Sync
items: Go to Settings > Cloud Sync
Tap 'Add Configuration' and enter your server URL, username, and password
Tap 'Test Connection' to verify the settings
Select this configuration as default
Tap 'Sync Now' to perform your first synchronization

sections.title: Sync Modes
sections.content: Sync Now: Performs bidirectional merge with automatic conflict resolution (newer version wins). Sync Data: Same as Sync Now but without uploading settings. Sync Config: Upload settings only. Force Upload: Overwrite cloud data with local data. Force Download: Overwrite local data with cloud data.

sections.title: Backup Protection
sections.content: Before each force upload or force download, the system automatically creates a local backup to prevent data loss. Force upload backs up the current cloud state first; force download backs up the current local state first. Config sync (upload/download settings) also auto-backs up.

sections.title: Backup Limits
sections.content: You can configure the max cloud backup count and max local backup count in sync settings (1-365, default 7). Oldest backups beyond the limit are automatically cleaned up.

Force Upload and Force Download are destructive operations. Force Upload will overwrite ALL cloud data with your local data. Force Download will delete ALL local data and replace it with cloud data. Use these only when you are certain of the direction you want to synchronize.
Sync also transfers your custom fonts and background images across devices. Media files are synchronized by SHA-1 hash to avoid re-uploading unchanged files.

items.question: Which WebDAV providers are supported?
items.answer: Any WebDAV-compatible server. Popular options include Jianguoyun (Nutstore), Nextcloud, ownCloud, and Synology WebDAV.

items.question: What data is synchronized?
items.answer: All cards, decks, knowledge bases, review logs, learning plans, splash quotes, settings, fonts, and media files.

items.question: How are conflicts resolved?
items.answer: During bidirectional sync, each entity has a version number. The entity with the higher version wins. This ensures that the most recent change on either device is preserved.

items.question: Sync fails with 'backup file not found'?
items.answer: If you experienced this on a previous version, upgrade to 0.26.15 or later. The issue has been fixed: backup path on Android now uses app internal storage.

sections.title: Backup Options
sections.content: LumeCard offers multiple ways to protect your data: automatic local backups during WebDAV sync, local file export/import, and automatic config backups during config sync.

sections.title: Automatic Local Backups
sections.content: Before each force sync operation, the system automatically creates a local backup. Force download backs up local data (shown in 'Local History'), force upload backs up cloud data (shown in 'Cloud History'). Config sync (upload/download settings) also auto-backs up.

sections.title: Exporting Data
items: Go to Settings > Data Management
Tap 'Export Data' to create a backup file (.json) with cards, decks, and knowledge bases
Choose a save location on your device

sections.title: Importing Data
items: Go to Settings > Data Management
Tap 'Import Data' and select a previously exported .json file
The imported data will be merged with your existing content (same-ID entities are overwritten)

sections.title: Restore History
sections.content: Restore history is split into two entries: 'Local History' shows local data backed up before force download, 'Cloud History' shows cloud data backed up before force upload. Each entry lets you restore data or config.

sections.title: Restore from Cloud
sections.content: The 'Restore from Cloud' feature downloads data from your WebDAV server and overwrites local data. It requires 3-step confirmation: first confirm -> confirm again -> manually type the confirmation word ('confirm' in English). Use with caution.

When importing data, entities with the same ID will be overwritten by the imported version. Restore from Cloud completely replaces local data with cloud data and cannot be undone. Create a backup before performing these operations.
You can configure backup limits in sync settings (1-365, default 7). Oldest backups beyond the limit are automatically cleaned up.

sections.title: Learning Settings
sections.content: Configure your daily learning goals: daily new card limit, daily review limit, and review mode (FSRS-6, SM-2, Leitner, or Simple). These settings affect how new cards are introduced and how review cards are scheduled.

sections.title: Appearance Settings
sections.content: Toggle dark mode, adjust font scale (70%-150%), and change the app language. Fonts: you can import custom .ttf or .otf font files and set them as the default card font.

sections.title: Study Timer
sections.content: The study timer tracks how much time you spend studying. You can configure it to pause when you are idle for a set duration, preventing inaccurate time tracking.
Learning Plans let you organize cards into structured study goals. Create a plan with specific decks or knowledge bases, track completion progress, and set default plans for quick access.

sections.title: Backup Limit Settings
sections.content: In Cloud Sync settings, you can configure the max cloud backup count and max local backup count (1-365, default 7). Cloud backups preserve cloud state before force upload; local backups preserve local state before force download. Oldest backups beyond the limit are automatically cleaned up.

items.question: Is LumeCard free?
items.answer: Yes, LumeCard is completely free and open source. There are no subscriptions or in-app purchases.

items.question: Can I use LumeCard on multiple devices?
items.answer: Yes, use WebDAV sync to keep your data synchronized across Android, Windows, Linux, and macOS devices.

items.question: Does LumeCard support Anki decks?
items.answer: LumeCard uses its own format. Direct Anki .apkg import is not currently supported, but you can use CSV import/export for data transfer.

items.question: What spaced repetition algorithm does LumeCard use?
items.answer: LumeCard uses FSRS-6 (21-parameter Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler) by default, with options for SM-2, Leitner, and Simple algorithms.

items.question: How do I reset a card's progress?
items.answer: Currently, individual card progress reset is not available. You can delete and recreate the card to start fresh.

items.question: Can I set different daily limits for different decks?
items.answer: Not currently. Daily limits are global settings. You can use Learning Plans to organize study sessions by topic.

items.question: Where is my data stored?
items.answer: Data is stored locally on your device. WebDAV sync stores an encrypted copy on your chosen cloud server.

items.question: How do I report a bug?
Does the app require an internet connection?
items.answer: No, LumeCard works fully offline except for AI features and WebDAV sync which require network access.

sections.title: Version 0.26.x
sections.content: Cloud sync backup overhaul: force upload backs up remote state, force download backs up local state. Restore history split into Local History and Cloud History. New Restore from Cloud with 3-step confirmation + manual input. Configurable backup limits (1-365, default 7). Export fixes (.json extension auto-append, knowledge base icon import). Android backup path fix (uses app internal storage). AI card generation event stream framework. Schema v3 (knowledge base icon field).

sections.title: Version 0.25.x
sections.content: FSRS-6 algorithm upgrade (21 parameters, trainable forgetting curve). Sample knowledge base (auto-created on first launch). Dashboard deck deletion. Card title field. Database migration to schema v2. Windows installer desktop shortcut option. Algorithm stability fixes (NaN crash, negative stability).

sections.title: Version 0.17.6
sections.content: WebDAV sync improvements with bidirectional version-based merge. Splash quote sync via WebDAV. Font deletion cleanup. Background image persistence. Startup animation fix.

sections.title: Version 0.17.2 - 0.17.5
sections.content: Unified Quote Settings screen with collapsible sections. Global settings search. Animation support for splash quotes. Screen saver mode with auto-exit on activity. Study timer idle pause.

sections.title: Version 0.16.x
sections.content: AI card generation with streaming support and event-driven architecture. Learning plans with completion tracking. Enhanced statistics.

sections.title: Version 0.15.x
sections.content: Initial WebDAV sync implementation. Multiple card types (Cloze, Multiple Choice). Splash quotes feature.

sections.title: Version 0.14.x
sections.content: FSRS algorithm integration. Basic study functionality. Deck and knowledge base management.

sections.title: Version 0.13.x - Earlier
sections.content: Initial project setup. Compose Multiplatform foundation. Database schema design.
